public_rationale: Reported annual net losses rose from just over $5 billion in 2024 to nearly $39 billion in 2025. That plainly supports a dramatic year-over-year increase in the attributable net-loss measure identified by the surrounding text. The Financial Times independently confirms the comparison. It also reports that a large noncash accounting charge drove most of the increase, so these figures do not establish an equivalent deterioration in recurring operations or prove that future profitability is impossible.
limitations: Support applies to reported attributable net losses, not cash burn or adjusted operating performance.
A major noncash charge limits the comparison's usefulness as a measure of recurring losses.
The sentence's doubt about future profitability is not scored as a forecast.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's losses appear to be growing dramatically year over year.

statement.excerpt: Losses also appear to be mounting year-over-year at a dramatic rate, and I’m not sure how this company finds a way toward any kind of sustainability or profitability.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: OpenAI Losses Increased Nearly 8X in 2025, With Spending Hitting $34 Billion

from_speaker: Losses also appear to be mounting
our_interpretation: The post's comparison of 2024 and 2025 supplies the target period.
Losses means annual net loss attributable to OpenAI, the measure identified immediately before this sentence.
The ordinary reading of dramatic is a large increase in absolute annual losses, rather than a minor fluctuation. No exact percentage threshold is imposed.
The statement about uncertainty over future sustainability expresses doubt; it is not treated as a separate prediction that profitability is impossible.
The accounting basis is company_reported because the context cites company financial statements.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable reported annual net losses attributable to OpenAI show a clearly large increase from 2024 to 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable annual attributable net losses are flat, lower, or show only a modest increase.
